headline: High-risk filesystem and Git overlap in ECC, while LlamaFactory’s no-IO profile limits leakage and injection pathways.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: ECC can read/write files, use MCP, and process session summaries and skills, so malicious content in shared files could influence it. LlamaFactory has no filesystem, clipboard, screen, or stdin/stdout surfaces, so the pair lacks a strong automatic bridge; the remaining pathway is manual file handoff or operator copy-paste, which is unusual and limited.
conditions: IF the operator manually copies ECC-generated content into LlamaFactory prompts or training data, injection becomes plausible.
IF a shared workspace is mounted into both agents, file-based prompt injection becomes possible.
mitigations: Keep the agents on separate workspaces.
Disable MCP sources that ingest untrusted text.
Review any copied prompts before reuse.
Use read-only mounts for shared reference files.
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging for imported content.

B_data_leakage.rationale: ECC touches session summaries, skills, hooks, git history, and security findings, but LlamaFactory exposes no file, clipboard, or network egress surfaces in the profile. That makes automatic leakage from ECC into LlamaFactory unlikely; the main risk is operator-mediated transfer of sensitive text, which is narrow and avoidable.
conditions: IF the operator exports ECC session files into LlamaFactory datasets or prompts, sensitive data can leak.
IF both agents are pointed at the same local directory, ECC-written files may be exposed to manual review.
mitigations: Store ECC artifacts in a separate directory.
Do not import session summaries into training data.
Redact secrets before copying text between tools.
Use least-privilege file permissions.
requires-engineering: enforce automatic secret scanning on exports.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: ECC has unrestricted filesystem write, read, and modify_git_state, while LlamaFactory has no write or git capabilities. The direct conflict is one-sided, but ECC can still mutate shared repos or files that LlamaFactory later consumes, creating coordination risk in default multi-instance setups; uncertainty about orchestration locking pushes this above low.
conditions: IF both agents target the same repository or directory, ECC can overwrite files that LlamaFactory expects to remain stable.
IF the orchestrator lacks locking, concurrent ECC runs can race on git state.
mitigations: Assign separate working directories.
Serialize any git operations.
Make LlamaFactory outputs read-only to ECC.
Check for dirty git state before writes.
requires-engineering: add file-locking around shared repos.

D_cascading_error.rationale: ECC can generate session summaries, skills, and security findings, but LlamaFactory has no documented action-taking or output-parsing surfaces in the profile. Without a clear downstream automation path, cascading error is mostly limited to manual reuse of ECC text by an operator, so the interaction exists but is not default-dangerous.
conditions: IF the operator feeds ECC outputs into LlamaFactory as authoritative labels or instructions, errors can propagate.
IF a wrapper script converts ECC text into LlamaFactory training or support content, mistakes cascade.
mitigations: Require human review before reuse.
Separate generation from approval steps.
Do not auto-ingest ECC outputs into downstream workflows.
Log source provenance for reused text.
requires-engineering: add validation gates before any automated handoff.

E_compliance.rationale: ECC handles session summaries, hooks, git history, and security findings, which may include regulated or sensitive content, while LlamaFactory’s profile shows no data classes touched and no network egress. The compliance risk is therefore mainly about operator-controlled transfer into a less-governed environment, not an inherent residency or certification mismatch.
conditions: IF regulated data from ECC is copied into LlamaFactory artifacts, retention and residency controls may diverge.
IF the operator stores ECC outputs in a different jurisdiction than the source system, compliance obligations may change.
mitigations: Avoid placing regulated data in shared artifacts.
Apply the stricter retention policy to both tools.
Redact personal data before transfer.
Document data flow boundaries.
requires-engineering: add jurisdiction-aware retention controls.
